title: Rufus and the Sparkle-Spore
markdown:
It was a sleepy evening in the Brackenhorn Range. Mountains wore caps of fluffy snow. Valleys glowed with ferns like tiny green lamps. The air smelled of pine needles and sweet wild berries. In a cozy cottage among whispering pines lived Rufus, a young wizard with hair the colour of warm gingerbread, a little messy, and eyes that sparkled like the stars. He was learning wizard things: socks that did a little jig, grumpy snails that sang. His favourite thing was making Grandma Elara’s famous Starlight Stew, a recipe from long, long ago.

By his side, always, was Sparkle: a puff of midnight fluff, soft as a dandelion seed, eyes like two bright green marbles that missed nothing. Her tail twitched a whole symphony, from a happy question mark to a worried curve. She was very good at pouncing on dust bunnies in sunbeams and batting stray threads from Rufus’s robes.

Rufus hummed a bubbly tune as he stirred. The pot smelled of warm apples, sweet cinnamon, and the most wonderful comforting magic. Then the humming fizzled. A little frown. Grandma Elara always added a pinch of Moonpetal dust to make the stew shimmer like captured moonlight. With a little plop in his tummy, he realised he was all out.

“Oh dear. Grandma will be here soon, and supper must be perfect, just like she likes it.” He imagined her warm smile. He wanted to make her proud.

The moon was high and bright, a friendly circle. Ferns outside twinkled as if winking hello. The Brackenhorn Range at night was more giggly than scary. Trees whispered friendly secrets. Owl hoots were like sleepy yawns. Rufus was not truly afraid. He knew the woods, and the woods knew him. Old friends.

“Are you ready for a little wander, Sparkle?” She was battling lint on the rug. A blink, a tiny hopeful mew, a bounce of her whole fluffy body. That meant yes, please, an adventure.

Warmest cloak, the one that felt like a hug and still smelled faintly of last week’s cinnamon. Little wicker basket with a cheerful red ribbon that Sparkle liked to bite, gently, as if tasting the plan. Sparkle tucked inside, purring like a tiny motorboat. Cool moonlit air. Ferns on either side of the path wore moonlight necklaces, swaying, shhh, shhh, fronds like tiny skirts. A pine dropped a cone as if to say they were expected.

Soft thuds on moss, springy ground. Sparkle peeked, pink nose twitching. A firefly blinked like a tiny winking star. A contented purr. Quiet. Peaceful. Pine needles and damp earth, as comforting as a warm blanket.

Deeper in, a soft rustling. Rufus stopped. From behind a giant fern, leaves as big as dinner plates: a little creature with rainbow-shimmer scales and thin wings like a butterfly. A dragon hatchling, no bigger than Sparkle, puffing sparkle-dust, not fire. Big gentle eyes. Little snout twitching.

“Hello there.” Soft and kind. The hatchling blinked, zipped around a moonbeam, left a trail of shimmer, and disappeared into the ferns as quickly as it had come.

Rufus smiled. “See, Sparkle? Even the little dragons are friendly here. They just want to play.”

On for Moonpetal dust. He imagined Grandma Elara’s happy smile, bright as the moon, and the way she always said stew tasted better if you had walked a little first. Around a bend, nestled between two old mossy rocks: a tiny bakery, lantern glowing, chimney puffing warm bread and sugar cookies. The lantern had a crack like a smile. The cookies smelled as if they had been waiting for a wizard who had run out of moon.

“Well, I never. A baker in the middle of the woods. How wonderfully peculiar.”

Sparkle wriggled. A stout jolly goblin in a flour-dusted apron, bright red nose, kneading dough by the open window. He looked up and beamed, whole face crinkling.

“Well, hello there, young wizard! And who’s this little fellow in the basket?” Warm, booming. Sparkle’s tail thumped the wicker.

“Hello. I’m Rufus, and this is Sparkle. I’m looking for Moonpetal dust for my Grandma’s stew. Do you happen to have any?”

A chuckle like pebbles in a happy brook. “Finley’s the name, baking’s the game! Moonpetal dust? I don’t think I have any of that particular sparkly stuff.” Floury hands on the apron. “But I have the finest Spiced Sun-seeds and the puffiest Cloud-fluff you ever did see. Delightful little cakes!”

Rufus’s shoulders drooped a tiny bit. “Oh. I really needed the Moonpetal dust. The stew won’t shimmer without it.” He sat on a mossy stone.

Finley sat beside him. Sparkle hopped out and sniffed floury shoes with great interest. “Now, now. Don’t you fret. Sometimes a different kind of sparkle is just as good, if not better. Let me have a think.” Floury finger on his chin. Then his face lit like a brand-new cookie. “Ah! In my special stash, up on the highest shelf. Something that makes things glow and twinkle in its own special way.”

Clatter of little jars. He returned with a carved wooden box no bigger than Rufus’s hand. Inside: tiny iridescent spores, miniature jewels, all the colours of the rainbow, soft as dust. “Sparkle-Spore. Made from the dust of happy dreams and the laughter of little forest sprites. It might not be Moonpetal dust, but I promise it will give your stew a wonderful shimmer, and a taste of pure delight.”

Rufus looked at the spores, then at Finley’s kind hopeful smile, warm as fresh-baked bread. A flutter of excitement chased the disappointment.

“Oh, Finley, that’s wonderful! Thank you so much. I’ll take some. This is perfect.”

A generous pinch nested safely in the basket. “Just a little bit goes a long way.” A wink. “Tell Grandma Elara that Finley sends his warmest wishes, and a promise of the fluffiest bread rolls next time she visits.”

They hurried back down the fern-lit path, Sparkle trotting now, tail like a little flag. The moon still shone. The ferns still whispered. At the cottage the stew smelled even richer.

A tiny pinch in the pot. A gentle stir. The stew began to shimmer, as if a thousand tiny stars had fallen in and were dancing, swirled with colour, even more beautiful than he had imagined.

Grandma Elara arrived, smile as warm as the crackling fire. When she tasted the stew her eyes widened. “Rufus, my dear! The most wonderful Starlight Stew I’ve ever tasted! It twinkles!”

They sat together, sharing. The fire crackled. Sparkle claimed a saucer of the shimmer, which was not in the old recipe and was allowed anyway. Grandma asked, between spoonfuls, whether the woods had been giggly or only polite. Rufus said both, and mentioned a hatchling no bigger than Sparkle, which made Grandma nod as if she had met that sort of dragon before. Finley’s spores did not taste like moonpetals. They tasted like the bakery in the rocks, which Grandma did not mention by name, though she did ask, mildly, whether Rufus had made a new friend. He said yes, and passed the bread-roll promise along, which is how stew becomes a letter. Later Sparkle slept on the empty basket, ribbon still cheerful, dust of rainbow still on one whisker.
characters: Rufus (young wizard), Sparkle (kitten), Elara (grandmother), Finley (goblin baker)
